item.title: AI Agents and Agentic AI in Medicine: An Autonomy-Centred Scoping Review and Research Agenda
item.description: Abstract Artificial intelligence agents—software systems that perceive, reason, plan and act over multiple steps with limited human intervention—are moving from research prototypes towards clinical deployment. Recent reviews map what has been built; this one asks what would have to hold for such systems to be deployed safely. item.title: Comment and Control: Hijacking Agentic Workflows via Context-Grounded Evolution
item.description: Automation platforms such as GitHub Actions and n8n are increasingly adopting so-called agentic workflows, which integrate Large Language Model (LLM) agents for tasks such as code review and data synchronization. item.title: What makes an LLM a tutor? A component-centric survey of LLM-based and agentic tutoring systems
item.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are reshaping intelligent tutoring systems (ITSs) by reducing authoring costs and enabling flexible interaction. However, effective tutoring requires more than fluent responses. It also depends on pedagogical control, domain grounding, learner modeling, interaction design, orchestration, and reliable evaluation. item.title: When to Delegate: A Measurement Study of Bounded Agent Teams for Personal Super Agents
item.description: Abstract Personal super agents coordinate many tools while remaining fast, safe, and accountable to one user. A popular design is a Router delegating to Workers. Recent work shows coordination can cost more than it returns, but transfer to personal agents—single-user context, side-effecting tools, cross-turn references, and refusals—is not established. item.title: Fine-Tuned Large Language Models for Theory-Aligned Social Science Content Analysis: Evidence From Collaborative Learning Discourse
item.description: Theory-based content analysis is central to social science research, but coding context-dependent interactional discourse remains difficult to scale. This study examines whether fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) can support theory-aligned, episode-level coding of complex social interaction, using socially shared metacognitive regulation (SSMR) in collaborative learning discourse as a demanding empirical case. item.title: Delegating or Doing? Understanding User Behavior in Hybrid Human–Agent Interfaces
item.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly embedded into applications, allowing users to complete tasks either through direct manipulation or by delegating actions to conversational agents. However, little is known about how users balance these modalities when both are available. item.description: Modern applications move data through databases, APIs, observability pipelines, and generative systems; each hop can create a new data object: a stored derivative, an agent's tool result, per-step logs. item.title: The Karmic cycle of reform: teacher-student interactions shaping persistent practices and pedagogical possibilities in Nepal's basic schools
item.description: Nepal’s school education system has seen repeated reform efforts over the past two decades, which are aiming to improve quality and equity and promote Learner-Centred Education (LCE). item.description: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. item.description: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. item.title: Can TDD improve the quality of LLM-migrated code? : A pilot study in an industrial context
item.description: The emergence of Large Language Models (LLM) has created new possibilities for automating software development, yet ensuring the quality of AI-generated code remains a major challenge.
